frequency_question: How often do historical secondary sanction threats against major foreign financial institutions for embargoed energy trade culminate in formal penalties within a 20-day observation window when specific precursor signals are active?
membership_rule: Includes any formal US Treasury designation or banking system cutoff of a top-tier foreign commercial bank explicitly citing prohibited energy transactions with sanctioned states. Excluded are warning statements, diplomatic demarches, and penalties against minor/boutique financial entities.

cases.name: Chinese entity sanctions under CAATSA/Iran sanctions (various minor entities)
Zhuhai Zhenrong company penalty (not a bank)

provenance_note: claims 120 cases from only 4 named (30.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 4 named instances of major enforcement/near-misses; estimated 120 rolling 20-day windows of peak diplomatic confrontation where precursor signals matched current state.
known_gaps: Classified or non-public Treasury enforcement actions and informal compliance settlements are omitted.
skeleton: Major enforcement actions against systemic financial institutions over energy embargoes across post-Cold War sanctions regimes, grouped by high-tension escalation cycles (Iran sanctions tightening phases 2010-2012, 2018-2020, 2023-2026). Total roughly 3 major banking-specific designations in high-enforcement decades, evaluated across roughly 120 rolling 20-day high-signal windows.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 120 potential decision windows where precursors were visible
validity_reason: Base rate reflects enduring institutional behavior of the US Treasury Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) and geopolitical friction dynamics with major powers, stable through the current decade.
